summary: The status row draws four of the register's fourteen official REPD statuses. Measured across all 7,680 records of this cut, those four reach 5,264; the other ten hold 2,416 records -- Application Refused 667, Revised 531, Application Withdrawn 420, Appeal Refused 295, Planning Permission Expired 227, Abandoned 221, Appeal Withdrawn 39, Decommissioned 9, Appeal Lodged 5, No Application Required 2 -- and not one of them could be selected. They were loaded, searchable, sortable and in the CSV, and ALL STATUS was the only view that held them. One labelled select in the status row now names all ten with their own counts, read from the payload, on exactly the pattern the technology row already settled on. ?status= answers for every one of them; the whitelist stops being a hand-kept list.
modification_note: populateStatuses() counts the register's own status values off the payload at boot, adds every one to STATUSES, and appends one label and one select to #status. Neither node carries .btn, so setButtonState's selector does not find them and the four tabs keep their own handler untouched. releaseWiderStatus() is the single place the select and the tabs are reconciled, and the tabs, CLEAR FILTERS and hydrateFiltersFromUrl all call it, so the control and the table cannot name different things. The control reuses the wider-fleet control's existing classes, so there is no CSS change and it inherits the same 44px floor on a phone. This is not a separate cut: it sets the spine's own status and calls the spine's own apply(), and nothing renders a second table. One tightening comes with it -- the status test moves from item.status.includes(status) to equality. Substring and equality agree exactly on the four tab values across all 7,680 records (2,232 / 282 / 1,910 / 840, leak zero), so no answer changes today; it is tightened because the control now reaches ten more values and 'Appeal Refused' inside 'Application Refused' is the pair a substring test would find the day one more is added.
